input: In this section, the performance of the centrifugal pump that has been installed to transfer water between two vessels located at grade is described in some detail. Operating at its designated duty point, the pump provides a flow of 26 m3 h-1 against a total head of 64 m, and the efficiency achieved at this point is 80%, which represents a strong performance for a machine of this type. The shaft power absorbed by the pump at the duty point has been determined as 5.7 kW, and in order to ensure reliable operation under a range of conditions, the driving motor has been rated 15% above this figure, thereby providing a useful safety margin. During the course of the acceptance testing, no cavitation whatsoever was detected, which is an encouraging outcome; nevertheless, it is important to keep in mind that the acceptance test was conducted over a period of 4 h and exclusively at the duty point itself. This means that, while the pump has clearly demonstrated its ability to meet the specified duty under the tested conditions, its behaviour across the wider operating envelope, including part-load and overload conditions, remains to be established, and further testing may well be advisable in due course in order to confirm performance under those circumstances as well. None of this detracts from the fact that the specified duty itself has been met and demonstrated in a satisfactory manner, and the figures that have been obtained provide a firm and useful reference point against which the results of any future testing programme can be compared in the months and years ahead.
target: A centrifugal pump moves water between two vessels at grade. At the duty point the flow is 26 m3 h-1 against a head of 64 m, with a pump efficiency of 80%. Shaft power at the duty point is 5.7 kW, and the motor is rated 15% above this value. No cavitation was detected in the acceptance test, which ran for 4 h at the duty point only. The result therefore covers one operating point. At that point the pump delivered the specified flow and head without cavitation, and the efficiency and shaft power are the values the energy consumption of the service follows from. Away from that point the record is empty: neither the flow at which cavitation begins nor the efficiency at part load has been measured, and the acceptance test cannot be read as evidence for either. For the point it ran at, the test record is complete: flow, head, efficiency, shaft power and the absence of cavitation are all stated there. The gap in the record is not a defect of the test but a boundary on its use, and the boundary lies exactly at the edge of the duty point. What the test does fix is the duty against which the motor was sized. The rating stands above the shaft power at the specified point by that margin, so a duty revised upward consumes the margin first, and a duty revised beyond it exceeds the motor. The pump is demonstrated at the specified duty and untested elsewhere, and any future change to the required flow or head is a change to the one point for which evidence exists. Any statement about the pump's behaviour elsewhere in its range will need its own test, run at the condition it describes.
